links.outcome: Tumor board concordance of grounded agent versus plain LLM
links.effect: Ablation: plain LLM 0% concordance (mean 4.1) vs full grounded agent 86.7% (mean 9.0); expert ratings 4.22 ± 0.063 vs 3.21 ± 0.39 (P = 0.0015) for gpt-oss-120b; hallucinations 2/664 (0.3%).
links.quote: The plain LLM baseline achieved 0% concordance across all 15 cases (mean score 4.1); the full agent achieved 86.7% concordance (mean score 9.0).

links.outcome: Prospective silent-trial concordance with tumor board decisions
links.effect: 1-month silent trial on 64 consecutive cases: 82.8% concordance (53/64), comparable to retrospective/external performance.
links.quote: HemaGuide achieved 82.8% concordance (53/64), with entity-group rates of 81.6% for lymphomas (31/38), 82.4% for PC dyscrasias (14/17) and 88.9% for leukemias (8/9) ( κ = 0.795) (Fig. 6c,d ).

links.outcome: Concordance at external second academic center without re-optimization
links.effect: External validation on 555 cases across 47 entities: 81.8% concordance (454/555); lymphomas 79.2%, PC dyscrasias 90.9%, leukemias 84.6%, nonmalignant 70.0%.
links.quote: This evaluation used the original HemaGuide configuration without local re-optimization, confirming that the decision logic is not overfit to a single institution’s document structure or therapeutic style.

links.outcome: Tumor board concordance with grounded, tool-constrained generation versus an ungrounded baseline
links.effect: Across 15 ablation cases, concordance increased from 0% (mean score 4.1) for the plain LLM to 86.7% (mean score 9.0) for the full agent. Grounding was evaluated within a multicomponent architecture.
links.quote: The plain LLM baseline achieved 0% concordance across all 15 cases (mean score 4.1); the full agent achieved 86.7% concordance (mean score 9.0).

links.outcome: Resident treatment-recommendation concordance with and without AI assistance
links.effect: Residents (n = 4) evaluated 30 cases. Unaided concordance was approximately 60%; HemaGuide-assisted residents achieved near-senior concordance and sometimes exceeded senior subspecialists. Overreliance was not assessed.
links.quote: Unaided residents matched the tumor board ground truth in approximately 60% of cases, whereas residents with HemaGuide support achieved near-senior concordance, and in some comparisons superior performance, relative to senior physicians assessing cases inside their primary disease expertise (Fig. 4e–g ).

links.outcome: Fabricated drugs, clinical facts, or treatment histories in AI recommendations
links.effect: Hallucinations occurred in 2 of 664 evaluated cases (0.3%), both in external validation; none occurred in the benchmark or silent trial. Effects on clinical actions were not evaluated.
links.quote: Hallucinations—fabricated drugs, clinical facts or treatment histories with no basis in the input data—were observed in 2 of 664 evaluated cases (0.3%), both in the external validation dataset; none occurred in the benchmark or silent trial cohorts.

links.outcome: Automated somatic variant classification errors against expert reference classifications
links.effect: Classification agreed with the reference for 56/70 variants; sensitivity was 0.88 and specificity 0.84. No expert likely oncogenic/oncogenic variant was classified as likely benign/benign.
links.quote: Using three clinically pragmatic bins (likely benign/benign (LB/B), variant of uncertain significance (VUS), likely oncogenic/oncogenic (LO/O)), HemaGuide concurred with the reference for 56/70 variants (Fig. 3b and Supplementary Table 6 ).
